counterfactual_missing_items: ascites or pleural effusion (would support Meigs syndrome)
positive filarial serology (would support filarial lymphedema)
acute onset or painful swelling (would suggest other etiologies)
decisive_items: imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm
a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
response.rationale: R4 directly matches the vignette's central diagnosis of ovarian neoplasm, supported by explicit text and imaging findings. C1 is a more specific but dependent completion of R4, making it the runner-up. Other candidates either represent secondary findings (R5), are explicitly ruled out (R3), are symptoms rather than the diagnosis (R7), or lack key diagnostic criteria (R2).

rejected.why: Lymphedema is a clinical finding, not the underlying diagnosis; it does not explain the adnexal mass.
Filarial infection was explicitly ruled out by negative serology.
Uterine fibroids are present but do not account for the adnexal mass or the primary concern.
Meigs syndrome requires ascites and pleural effusion, which are absent; the diagnosis is speculative.
